newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Oct 11.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Oct 11.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Super League believes that it will be too much for stars of the Australian Rugby League competition to sit and watch an international competition and not be swayed to join the new world cup run by Super League. Page 22.

The National Netball League will form the top netball players from five states into an eight-team national league from next year onwards. The NNL will have two clubs from Sydney, Melbourne and Adelaide and one from each of Perth and Brisbane. Page 21.

Socceroos coach Eddie Thomson wants to keep his job after Australia's 0-0 draw with Saudi Arabia in Riyadh yesterday. Thomson is currently being looked at by Japanese J-League club Hiroshima and wants to resolve his situation quickly. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Parramatta last night decided to turn down Super League's offer of joining its competition, supporting the Australian Rugby League. However, the Eels stated that the door remained open on joining the Super League competition in 1998. Page 42.

Australian Rugby League chief executive John Quayle yesterday struck out at politicians from both sides of parliament, stating that both major parties had attempted to influence the ARL clubs to join the News Ltd sponsored Super League. Page 42.

Australia's cricket team is feeling the loss of three of its best players in its Test match against India. They were bowled out for 182, their lowest scoring effort since being sent out for 128 by the West Indies. Page 42.
THE AGE

Sydney Swans forward Anthony Rocca's unorthodox declaration to join Collingwood or nothing for A$250,000 a year has put pressure on the AFL to charge him with conduct prejudicial to the draft. Page C8.

West Coast has made a last minute claim to 17-year old Claremont ruckman Michael Gardiner for next year's line up. The deal was made only hours after Hawthorn's attempt to traded Nick Holland to Port Power was abandoned. Page C8.
Australia suffered a spin lead attack and faltered for only 182 runs in their first match against India yesterday. Only one of the Australians' wickets fell to a seam bowler - the first. Page C8.
HERALD SUN

Carlton has traded two draft choices and gained former Collingwood star Michael McGuane who will turn 29 this year. With the club's poor performance this year and its average player age of 26, it was expected that the club would aim for younger players. Page 102.

Shane Heal, who is bound to the NBA next year to play for the Minnesota Timberwolves for A$1.8 million, is the latest star to be signed to the Nike sports label. Such a signing could earn Heal up to A$55,000 a year. Page 102.

Champion Irish jockey Michael Kinane was confirmed as the rider for Oscar Schindler yesterday - a horse he believes is superior to 1993 winner Vintage Crop and a good chance at winning this year's Melbourne Cup. Page 102.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

St George and Parramatta have pledged their support to the Australian Rugby League competition. The boards of both clubs were offered individual franchises worth over A$25 million over five years by News Limited to join the Super League competition. Page 112.
Australia has stumbled in its one day Test match against India, going down with only 182 runs on the first day. India at stumps yesterday, had 57 runs for only one out, Vikram Rathore. Page 110.

The Sydney City Roosters have decided to stay in the Australian Rugby League, yesterday signing on with the ARL for another year of competition. The Roosters will be one of the powerful teams in next year's ARL competition. Page 108.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
